titles: Run the palette's solver checks in the page, not only in a terminal
Run the palette's solver checks in the page on the hosted site too (optional)
first_title: Run the palette's solver checks in the page, not only in a terminal
first_body: - [ ] **Run the palette's solver checks in the page, not only in a terminal.** `verify`, `consistency`, `refine`, `bounds` and `fault-tree` are in the registry (`src/ui/checks.ts`) but report `not here` with a copyable command, because z3 needs a cross-origin-isolated page and this one is not. Decide how to get isolation (COOP/COEP headers from the dev and preview servers, and whatever the static host allows), then let the registry's `solver` entries run through `z3-bridge` when `crossOriginIsolated` is true. A check that cannot run must keep saying so rather than passing.
last_body: - [ ] **Run the palette's solver checks in the page on the hosted site too (optional).** Since N6 S4 the dev and preview servers send `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` (`SYSPROSE_NO_ISOLATION=1` turns them off for local Google Drive testing), and the palette's five solver checks run z3 in the page there and land in the Checks tab. The GitHub Pages site cannot send the headers and decision U14 ruled out a service worker, so on it they keep `not here` with the copyable command. Done only by moving the model site to a host that sends the headers, which would break the Google Drive sign-in popup and Picker iframe there too. Awaits user decision U14 (host): whether in-page z3 on the hosted site is worth that cost. [N6 S4] DECIDED 2026-10-23 (U14): decide after Drive (U16); until then the hosted site keeps `not here` with the copyable command.

first_title: Scope the palette's checks to the selection where the CLI takes --element

titles: Let a check run off the main thread when it is slow
first_title: Let a check run off the main thread when it is slow
first_body: - [ ] **Let a check run off the main thread when it is slow.** Every `model` check is synchronous today, which is right for the sample model (each is well under a frame) but not for a large one: `reach` and `check-behaviour` walk configuration graphs. Measure first, then move the walkers into the worker the solver lane already uses.
last_body: - [ ] **Let a check run off the main thread when it is slow.** Every `model` check is synchronous today, which is right for the sample model (each is well under a frame) but not for a large one: `reach` and `check-behaviour` walk configuration graphs. Measure first, then move the walkers into the layout worker (`src/ui/elk-worker.ts`), the only Web Worker today — the solver lane has none. Cost ≈ configurations × (|alphabet| + 1) × |region transitions| × stack depth: `stepCandidates` scans every region transition per configuration and input, and `check-behaviour` walks twice per property, so `maxConfigs` does not bound the time.

titles: Never put a user element inside a library root
first_title: Never put a user element inside a library root
first_body: - [ ] **Never put a user element inside a library root.** `createElement` (owner falls back to the selection), `reparent` and `reparentMany` take a library element as owner, e.g. with the Explorer's library toggle on. Such an element has no `isLibrary` flag but sits under a library root, so the Text view, Save to Drive and Export ▾ → SysML all leave it out, while model JSON keeps it. Nor does an edit to it read unsaved — what is saved is compared as text — so New, Open ▾ and Import drop it without asking, though a Save in this browser would have kept it. Refuse a library owner, or fall back to the root.

titles: Give the focus somewhere safe when a rename closes on Enter
Give the focus somewhere safe when a rename closes on Escape
Give the focus somewhere safe when the Requirements table's reference picker closes
first_title: Give the focus somewhere safe when a rename closes on Enter
first_body: - [ ] **Give the focus somewhere safe when a rename closes on `Enter`.** `Enter` in the Explorer's rename (`tree-rename`), the context menu's (`node-ctx-rename-input`) or a Requirements table cell (`req-cell-input`, `req-attr-input`) commits and closes the box, and the focus falls to the page (to the canvas node, for the context menu): the next `Backspace` deletes the selection — the element just renamed, with its subtree — and a digit switches the view. Undo brings it back. `Ctrl/⌘+S` in those boxes already leaves the focus on Save (`focusSave`, `src/ui/commands.ts`); do the same after `Enter`, or return it to the row, guarded.
last_body: - [ ] **Give the focus somewhere safe when the Requirements table's reference picker closes.** Since `ui-small` S2 `Escape` in the Explorer's rename, the context menu's and a Requirements cell leaves the focus on Save (`cancelAndFocusSave`, `src/ui/commands.ts`). `Escape` in the picker (`req-ref-picker`) and `Enter` on a candidate close it with the focus dropped to the page, and a pick selects the requirement row, so the next `Backspace` deletes the requirement just linked. Route the keydown paths (not the blur, which cancels) through `cancelAndFocusSave` / `commitAndFocusSave`. Check the Regroup view's bundle-label and port-name boxes (`RegroupView.tsx`, the Enter and Escape handlers that call `blur()`), which from code reading also leave the focus on the page. Done when `Escape` and `Enter` in the picker leave a following `Backspace` harmless, with a test. [ui-small S2, review]

titles: Show the strip's note beside its status row, not in place of it
first_title: Show the strip's note beside its status row, not in place of it
first_body: - [ ] **Show the strip's note beside its status row, not in place of it.** With Google Drive configured, any `info` notice — a save or an export that kept typed text back, an element sent to the top level of the model — outranks the rows for a save waiting on a sign-in (`expired`), a file in the trash or read-only (`gone`, `readonly`), unsaved changes (`dirty`) and being offline (`driveStripStatus`, `src/ui/panels/DriveStrip.tsx`), until it is hidden or Undone: the row that says the file lacks the model is not shown. In the other direction `sayWhatWasKept` puts nothing up while an unrelated notice stands (a Drive error, `<name> closed`), so an export that kept typed text back leaves the file lacking it unsaid. Render the note on a line of its own under the row, and hold the export's until the strip is free.

titles: Keep text typed in the Text view when a field's change is applied
first_title: Keep text typed in the Text view when a field's change is applied
first_body: - [ ] **Keep text typed in the Text view when a field's change is applied.** An edit in the app re-serialises the Text view over text typed there and not applied (`recomputeNow` with `forceText`, `src/ui/store.ts`), so a Properties box left — or `Ctrl/⌘+S` typed in it — while the Text view reads *modified — not yet applied* drops that text with no note and no Undo. first_title: Let the palette's check-behaviour check the machine its command names

titles: Stop a composite state's last-active child from multiplying the configurations a walk keeps
first_title: Stop a composite state's last-active child from multiplying the configurations a walk keeps
first_body: - [ ] **Stop a composite state's last-active child from multiplying the configurations a walk keeps.** `hashConfig` (`src/semantics/mc/config.ts`) puts the history map into the visited-set key, and `exitTo` records the last-active child of every composite it leaves, so the configurations of a machine multiply with its composites: five composites of 3 to 4 substates (24 states) reach `reach`'s 10,000-configuration bound (`docs/TEST-REPORT.md` §2.15), where a flat machine of 24 states has 24. Only a history composite ever reads the map (`enterCascade`), and `exploreMachine` refuses those machines (`history-state`, unsupported), so for every machine it walks the map is dead state in the key. Leave it out of the key when the machine has no history composite and see what moves: every `configs` figure and `after N configuration(s)` sentence of a machine with composites (goldens in `test/unit/semantics.mc.*` and `test/campaign`, the user guide's reach sections), and the machines that now finish inside the bound and so publish their unreachable and dead lists where they said *undecided*. Tried once, with the map left out of the key and nothing else changed: the flight controller of §2.15 walks 19 configurations in 3 ms and `reach` decides; a generated machine of five composites whose every substate also exits to a top state still reaches the bound, so something else multiplies there and wants finding. The palette's worker (`src/ui/checks-worker.ts`) already keeps such a walk off the page; this removes the walk. Fixtures to re-make and figures to re-measure when it lands, since they rely on a machine that still hits the bound: `test/unit/checks-registry.test.ts` (*give a machine at the walk's bound…* asserts `reach` is `undecided` on five composites), `test/e2e/palette-checks.sp

titles: Keep a layered General view's column headers on screen while panning down a column
first_title: Keep a layered General view's column headers on screen while panning down a column
first_body: - [ ] **Keep a layered General view's column headers on screen while panning down a column.** A header (`src/ui/panels/ColumnHeaders.tsx`) is drawn once, above the top of its piece, so in the drone-swarm model's whole General view (columns about 19,000 px tall) it is off screen at every zoom where the boxes read. Pin it to the canvas's top edge while its piece runs beneath it, clamped to the piece; decide how it then stays clear of the boxes under it. titles: Cut the crossings the hub-led layout leaves in the drone-swarm v9 OA General view
first_title: Cut the crossings the hub-led layout leaves in the drone-swarm v9 OA General view
first_body: - [ ] **Cut the crossings the hub-led layout leaves in the drone-swarm v9 `OA` General view.** The view has 31 crossings in the app's readability count (46 in the layout's own count, `countCrossings`), down from 71 and 88 in those two counts, with the two members drawn as hubs. Of the 46, 26 are two `«allocate»` lines crossing, 9 an `«allocate»` and a `«satisfy»`, 7 an `«allocate»` and a `«typed-by»`: the two members' activities share one definition per step, so the two fans interleave. Try ordering the activities of the two fans by their shared definition (barycentre), or letting only one member lead.
last_body: - [ ] **Cut the crossings the hub-led layout leaves in the drone-swarm v9 `OA` General view.** The view has 46 crossings in the layout's own count (`countCrossings`, `src/diagram/layout.ts:531`), down from 88 before the hub-led layout; `memberA` and `memberB` (14 allocations each) and `dutyController` (3) are drawn as hubs. d60cd5d measured 31 crossings, down from 71, in the app with real text widths; that figure was not re-measured at 5943654. Of the 46, re-counted at 5943654: 26 are two «allocate» lines crossing, 9 an «allocate» and a «satisfy», 7 an «allocate» and a «typed-by», 4 two «typed-by» lines: the two members' activities share one definition per step, so the two fans interleave. SA and LA are at 0. Try ordering the activities of the two fans by their shared definition (barycentre), or letting only one member lead. Done when the OA count is below 46 with no overlap or line through a box introduced.

titles: Give tied centrality scores one rank
first_title: Give tied centrality scores one rank
first_body: - [ ] **Give tied centrality scores one rank.** Properties shows `Centrality … #N of 1373` (`elementCentrality`, `src/diagram/centrality.ts`). It orders equal scores by element id, and ids are random UUIDs (`newId`, `src/core/ids.ts`), so a tied element's rank changes with every load: the drone-swarm v9 root package (score 0.0004) read #973, #852, #1188 and #1067 in four loads of the same file, so tutorial stills that show a tied element's rank differ from one recording to the next. Give tied scores the best rank they share (competition ranking), or show *tied*, or break the tie by qualified name, which a load does not change.

first_title: Take no event where a completion transition is enabled or undetermined, or reword the run warrant
first_body: - [ ] **Take no event where a completion transition is enabled or undetermined, or reword the run warrant.** `reach` and `check-behaviour` walk every trigger at every configuration while the machine's own semantics fires a completion transition before any event, so a `fail` or `covered` witness, a `no way out`/`choice` row, or an undecided guard can claim a run the profile forbids (`rc/a15`, `rc/a1`, `rev/r8`, the v9 SA `recallWhileTransiting` case, and completion livelocks). Until the engine and the CLI agree, the app's `rtc-gap.ts` demotes the unconfirmed rows to walk-only; delete that confirmation in the same change.

titles: Read a package-level or definition-feature binding
Read a package-level or definition-feature binding, and a redefined bound usage (w4, R13, R13b)
first_title: Read a package-level or definition-feature binding
first_body: - [ ] **Read a package-level or definition-feature binding.** A `bind` written at package level or between two definition features (probe `w4`) is left unread per instance — every surface abstains — so the value it carries never decides a row; the connector is outside the per-instance frame walk (H5).
last_body: - [ ] **Read a package-level or definition-feature binding, and a redefined bound usage (`w4`, R13, R13b).** A `bind` written at package level or between two definition features (probe `w4`) is left unread per instance, so the value it carries never decides a row (`W4::c2` reads ?/?/?/? with no ref; the intended ref is F), and the connector is outside the per-instance frame walk. The same family: `part pp :>> p` redefining a bound usage (`R13` and `R13b`, ?/?/?/? beside refs T and F). 075b306 (reverted by ab965c7) had `featureAtPath` and `boundSourceIn` read it and reached R13/R13b T/T/T/? and F/F/F/? and W4 `c2` F/F/F/?, missing the SMT row. Reuse those two and add the SMT side. Done when `W4::c2` reads F/F/F/F and R13/R13b read T/T/T/T and F/F/F/F. [review 2026-10-14 E2, E8] Builds on the H5 entry above; awaits user decision U6 for W4's ref.

first_title: Decide what the layout does with a piece that nests (P1)
first_body: - [ ] **Decide what the layout does with a piece that nests (P1).** `layoutOptionsFor(viewKind, nested)` (`src/diagram/layout.ts:105`) sets `elk.hierarchyHandling: 'INCLUDE_CHILDREN'` for a piece that has a nested box and `SEPARATE_CHILDREN` for every other piece (`214b3c5`; `toElkTree` computes `nested`, `:417`), so only the flat case was fixed. Through `layoutDiagram` on the `interconnection` view, 30 parents of 10 children and two edges per leaf (330 nodes) take 11 113 ms at 5943654 against 171 ms with `SEPARATE_CHILDREN` forced (65x); a reviewer's run on a loaded machine read 26 924 ms against 299 ms. ELK runs in a Web Worker (`src/ui/elk-worker.ts`), so the page does not freeze, but the diagram appears no sooner. On the drone-swarm v9 the option is not the dominant cost (General 5 035 ms against 4 469 ms forced, `interconnection` 550 against 486, `tree` 44 184 against 42 411; one run each). Either drop the option for nested pieces, which trades the layout of edges that cross a parent's border for time, or bound the compound layout. Done when that case lays out within a time the decision names, measured through `layoutDiagram` (`U diagram.layout2` asserts the option for a flat and a nested call, not the time). `docs/UI-ROADMAP.md` P1 has the table. Awaits a user decision, not yet numbered in the plan: drop the option for nested pieces, or bound the compound layout.
last_body: - [ ] **Decide what the layout does with a piece that nests (P1, U19).** `layoutOptionsFor(viewKind, nested)` (`src/diagram/layout.ts`) sets `elk.hierarchyHandling: 'INCLUDE_CHILDREN'` for a piece that has a nested box and `SEPARATE_CHILDREN` for every other piece. N6 S2 measured both through `layoutDiagram` at `aac38fd` (the table is in `docs/UI-ROADMAP.md` P1): the profile's 11 s reproduces on the entry's own 330-node graph (43–45 s shipped on a loaded machine, 0.6–1.4 s forced, 69×), so the time rule is met there, but forcing `SEPARATE_CHILDREN` lays each parent's interior out alone and does not route an edge that crosses a parent's border (576 of that graph's 600 edges are drawn as straight lines through boxes); on a structured variant it is only 4.6–5.8× faster with 20% more crossings and 300 unrouted edges, and on the real v9 views it changes nothing. So no layout code changed. What stays open is to bound the compound layout: lay each parent's interior out on its own, then route the border-crossing edges ourselves. Done when the 330-node case lays out within a time the decision names, measured through `layoutDiagram`, with no unrouted edge and no more crossings than the shipped option on the structured variant. titles: Settle whether a drag-pan closes a canvas context menu, and delete the sentence that is wrong
first_title: Settle whether a drag-pan closes a canvas context menu, and delete the sentence that is wrong
first_body: - [ ] **Settle whether a drag-pan closes a canvas context menu, and delete the sentence that is wrong.** `docs/UI-ROADMAP.md` says both that wheel-zoom and pan dismiss the fixed-position menu (Shipped, *Context menus close when the canvas moves*) and that the menus do not dismiss when the canvas is panned (Known limitations). `E gui-context-menu` drives a wheel only. `useContextMenuChrome` (`src/ui/panels/useContextMenuChrome.ts`) closes on a canvas wheel, on Escape and on a window `mousedown` outside the menu, and its comment calls a pan a pane mousedown "already handled by `onDown`"; but d3-zoom's `mousedowned` stops the propagation of the mousedown it takes for a pan, so `onDown` may never see it. Open a node's context menu in the built app, drag the pane, and see whether the menu is gone. Then delete the wrong sentence in the roadmap (and fix the hook's comment if that is the wrong one) and add the pan to `gui-context-menu`. Done when the two sentences agree and the spec drives a pan.

titles: Hold the redefined feature's default at an instance wherever a held implicit end copy redefines it
first_title: Hold the redefined feature's default at an instance wherever a held implicit end copy redefines it
first_body: - [ ] **Hold the redefined feature's default at an instance wherever a held implicit end copy redefines it.** `holdDefault` (`src/semantics/defining-equation.ts:2665-2684`) adds the instance to `heldIn` only when the end copy itself writes a default (`:2683`), so a held copy with no default leaves the redefined feature's default standing at the instance and SMT's axiom for it contradicts the binding: soundness decision 10 (a binding overrides a default in its context, on every surface) is broken. Probe (A4, the review's `A/probes/a4-second-binding.sysml`): the A2 model, `q1` included, with `q2` replaced by `part q2 : Q { attribute E = 20.0; bind p.extra = E; }` in package `A4`: `P::c in A4::q2::p` reads T/T/T/X where it is F (1 + 20 > 10), and the own row `A4::P::c` went from T×4 to T/T/T/X, a new I7 case (re-run at 5943654: `verify --engine literal` discharges all four rows and `--engine smt` answers `inconsistent-axioms` on all four). Fix: hold the default at the instance whenever an implicit end copy is held, even if it writes none (a valueless copy that redefines a feature an asserted equation defines, GA6's `p.load`, must keep reading the assert), and stop the instance value row asserting a default a binding overrides there. first_title: Treat a capped binding's whole connector component as past the cap
first_body: - [ ] **Treat a capped binding's whole connector component as past the cap.** `boundSourceIn` (`src/semantics/defining-equation.ts:3165`; its cap test `:3205`), `defaultStandsIn` (`:3311`) and `holdEnds` (`:2475`; caps recorded `:2553`, `:2559`) treat only the capped pair as past-cap, so a capped binding's value that reaches a feature through a second, uncapped binding is read as that feature's default. Present at 7277a97 as well. Probe (CAP1, the review's `A/probes/cap1-per-binding.sysml`), a generated chain in `package CAP`: `part def T0 { attribute load : ScalarValues::Real default = 1.0; attribute m2 : ScalarValues::Real = 10.0 - load; }`, `part def T1 { attribute L : ScalarValues::Real default = 1.0; part a : T0; bind a.load = L; }`, `part def Tn { part a : T(n-1); }` for n = 2 to 33, `part top : T33;`, then `attribute X : ScalarValues::Real = 50.0; bind top.a.….L = X;` (32 times `.a`, so the binding is written 33 usages deep) and `attribute Y : ScalarValues::Real default = 1.0; bind Y = top.a.….load;` (33 times `.a`) with `constraint yT { Y >= 40.0 }` and `constraint yF { Y <= 5.0 }`. titles: Index the per-instance machinery so the check meets its performance targets
first_title: Index the per-instance machinery so the check meets its performance targets
first_body: - [ ] **Index the per-instance machinery so the check meets its performance targets.** `instanceGroups` (`src/semantics/defining-equation.ts:3400`) and `instancesOfDefinition` (`:3359`) are uncached (the plan's `INSTANCE_GROUPS` per (model, rev) does not exist), `boundSourceIn` (`:3165`) scans every reading per symbol, and `componentConnectors` (`:3092`) walks `model.all()` per call. Measured at 5943654: paired in-process against 7277a97, big-bind-600 (the `big-bind-N` builder of `test/unit/semantics.solver.test.ts:182`) went 721 → 35,934 ms (target 700), tree10 41 → 22,008 ms, perf9b 34 → 5,251 ms (target 300), big-bind-1200 takes 90.9 s (target 1 s); the CLI `sysml-check` takes 13.2 s on big-bind-600 and 6.5 s on perf9b; perf9b's Problems tab holds 1,568 Solve rows (cap 200). The app runs this check on every edit. Fix: cache `instanceGroups` per (model, rev), build the package-denote index once, index readings by instance prefix for `boundSourceIn`, and memoise `classified` and the connectors per (root, component). Probe (m1, the review's `E/pi/m1.sysml`): `package H { part def P { attribute load default = 1.0; constraint c { load <= 10.0 } } part def Q { attribute L default = 1.0; part p : P; bind p.load = L; } }` and eight usages `part qN : Q { attribute :>> L = 50.0; }` (N = 1 to 8): all the violated-instance findings sit at `part p : P` in `Q` (`3:64` when the package, `P` and `Q` each take a line), none at a `:>> L` (re-run at 5943654). Fix: set `anchorId` to the differing redefinition or stated member when the group row is built. Done when m1's findings anchor at each usage's `:>> L` line. [review 2026-10-14 PI-2]

titles: Route a binding-carried context read to constraint-by-instance
first_title: Route a binding-carried context read to constraint-by-instance
first_body: - [ ] **Route a binding-carried context read to `constraint-by-instance`.** The per-instance plan sends a context read that goes through a binding (h2c, k2, M7) to `validation/constraint-by-instance`. Those reads do not get the `via` flag (`via` is set only where `boundAbove` finds a binding above the context, `src/semantics/evaluate-model.ts:1397`), so they pass the filter of `target-by-specialisation` (`src/validation/rules.ts:1028`: `via !== true && instance === undefined`) and are reported with that code, anchored at the definition feature. mbse-workflow treats `target-by-specialisation` as REPORTED_ONLY ("do not change an estimate to meet it"), the guidance the plan's H3 rejected. Probe (h2c, the review's `E/pi/h2c.sysml` without its second usage): `package H2C { part def P { attribute load default = 1.0; attribute m2 = 10.0 - load; } part def Q { attribute L default = 1.0; part p : P; bind p.load = L; constraint c { p.m2 >= 0.0 } } part q : Q { attribute :>> L = 50.0; } }`: `sysml-check` prints `validation/target-by-specialisation q::p.m2 = -40 misses Q::c` and no `constraint-by-instance` (re-run at 5943654). Fix: mark any binding-carried context read as an instance reading, and re-check mbse-workflow's code notes against the new routing. Done when h2c, k2 and M7 emit `constraint-by-instance`. [review 2026-10-14 PI-3]

titles: Take the minimum over a requirement's per-reading records when writing its case verdict
first_title: Take the minimum over a requirement's per-reading records when writing its case verdict
first_body: - [ ] **Take the minimum over a requirement's per-reading records when writing its case verdict.** `evidence-attach` writes the case verdict after attaching (`scripts/sysprose.ts:3347`, `writeCaseVerdicts`), but `judgedFromRecords` (`:3203`) looks the requirement up by name and cannot find the `R in X` name a per-instance relation carries, and `writeVerdict` (`src/semantics/verify.ts:864`) takes the case's verdict from the records it does find. Probe (h5): a requirement `LoadReq` verified by `VC` over two readings, p1 with load 50 (refuted) and p2 proved: `verify --engine smt --record`, then `evidence-attach` prints `H::LoadReq — verdict fail → pass from H::VC` and writes `verdict = "pass"` over a live refuted v2 carrier; every re-attach flips it again (`evidence-status` flags it as `verdict-overstates-evidence`). Fix: map `instance.requirement` back and take the minimum over the per-reading records, or have `writeVerdict` take the worse of the two. Done when the h5 probe ends `fail` after attach and stays `fail` on every re-attach, with v9's records, attach output and status unchanged (83 records, 49 attached, 34 skipped). [review 2026-10-14 EV-1]

titles: Never let the load health vouch for a text that does not load
first_title: Never let the load health vouch for a text that does not load
first_body: - [ ] **Never let the load health vouch for a text that does not load.** `loadHealth` (`src/ui/store.ts:4231`) trusts a serializer-side signal (`serializeUserModelSignals`, `src/text/health.ts:163`) and skips the parse of a text it calls reference-faithful (`textHealthOf`, `store.ts:4214`). The signal's `parseErrorsOf` (`health.ts:87-103`) checks only references and the `value` text, so a typo in a guard, trigger, effect, expression or metadata, a non-string value, a raw newline in a quoted value and a name or unit holding a newline all read as 0 errors; `valueTextParses` (`health.ts:106-120`) accepts a value such as `2; attribute rate = 3` that parses alone while the whole text gets two validation errors; and a user-referenced package flagged `isLibrary` is vouched for [LH-1, LH-3]. `rememberText` (`store.ts:955-961`) also lets the signal's count overwrite a parsed one, so a faulty line applied in the Text view goes from 1 error to 0 and a fallback parse is undone by the next `loadHealth()` (5/4 becomes 1/0); Drive and file opens take the same path [LH-2]. Probe: on `state a; state b; state final; transition t1 first a then b; transition t2 first b then final;` set the effect of `t1` to `}` in Properties: health reports 0 errors and Reachability reads `holds`, while the saved text makes `reach` exit 1. Fix, either way recording whether a memo entry came from a parse or from the signal and never letting a signal replace a parse: (a) always parse: parse each distinct text once, memoised by text, in the checks worker so the page does not stall, and let the signal skip validation only; or (b) keep the parse-free certificate and make it re-read every verbatim field in its grammatical slot, refuse a name or unit holding a newline, count non-string values and require exactly

titles: Emit containment in pre-order wherever a model is serialised
first_title: Emit containment in pre-order wherever a model is serialised
first_body: - [ ] **Emit containment in pre-order wherever a model is serialised.** `Model.reparent` appends the child to its new owner (`src/core/model.ts:430-432`) while `rebuildIndex` (`:519-534`) groups children by insertion order, so `toJSON` and `toJSONWhere` (`:562-571`) emit them out of containment order. The checks worker's `userPart` (`src/ui/checks-offthread.ts:91-101`), Save in this browser (`store.ts:3418`) and every Undo snapshot (`store.ts:1822`, `:3814`, `:3837`) rebuild a model whose children are reordered, and an initial-less composite state takes its first child as its initial one (`initialState`, `src/semantics/mc/config.ts:563-566` at 5943654). Probe: a machine with `initial start`, a composite `Work { Prep; Run }` with no `initial`, and the property `absence globally "state Spare"`; drag the older state `Spare` into `Work` in the Explorer: the page's check-behaviour reads `holds` (1 pass) and the worker's `issues` (1 fail), `reach` gives 3 configurations and 2 findings on the page against 2 and 4 in the worker, and Save then reopen, or any Undo, rewrites the Text view from `state B; state C; state A;` to `state A; state B; state C;`. Fix: emit user elements in containment pre-order (a DFS over the children from the user roots) in `toJSON`, `toJSONWhere` and `userPart`. Done when tests show that after a reparent the worker matches the page (verdict, configurations, findings), Save then reopen keeps the order and an initial-less composite's initial state, and Undo after a reparent restores the text byte for byte. [review 2026-10-14 D-1, D-2]

first_title: Model the interpreter's 64-step completion budget in the walk and the search
first_body: - [ ] **Model the interpreter's 64-step completion budget in the walk and the search.** `runStateMachine` (`src/semantics/execute.ts`) follows an event with trigger-less (completion) steps for at most 64; a chase that spends the budget stops where it is and the next event is taken from there (`completionBudgetHit`). Since `0c9d2bd` the walk offers no event at a configuration where a completion transition is enabled (`src/semantics/mc/explore.ts:1103-1105`) and the property search does the same (`patterns.ts:1161-1163`), and the chase counter is set when a configuration is first found (`explore.ts:1179`, `:1192`), so a revisit never trips it. On a cycle of completions, or a chain longer than the budget, the walk misses runs the interpreter takes: `unreachable`, `dead`, a safety PASS and `not-covered` can be false, and the comment at `explore.ts:941` ("a completion cycle is not a bound hit") argues the wrong way [C1]. Separately, the search tests the monitor for a violation (`patterns.ts:1201`) before it applies the chase-budget gate (`:1218`), so a `cover` prints COVERED, with a witness, for a state the interpreter never enters [H2]. (2) A generated chain: states `s0`, `c1`…`c70` and `z`, `go first s0 accept go then c1`, `t<n> first c<n> then c<n+1>` for n = 1…69, `ju

titles: Cut what an edit costs the page on the drone-swarm v9 model
Divide the text step and the edit's own task on the drone-swarm v9 model
first_title: Cut what an edit costs the page on the drone-swarm v9 model
first_body: - [ ] **Cut what an edit costs the page on the drone-swarm v9 model.** Each edit's recompute (`recomputeNow`, `src/ui/store.ts`) validates the whole model and writes its text on the page's thread before the diagram is rebuilt: one task, after every edit, whether or not a check is run, of 0.14 to 0.63 s on v9 in a browser, the longer the more loaded the machine (load averages from about 4 to about 20; in node, validation about 0.35 s and the text 0.15 to 0.3 s). A palette check's click no longer runs it ahead of time (branch `load-health` S3: the run begins first and reads the load once its row is drawn, `runCheckedOnceDrawn`), but the page still stops for it after each edit, and the `E palette-checks` guard on v9 leaves that task out as the edit's. Fix: validate only what an edit can change, write the text in a worker, or both, measured on v9 first. Done when an edit on v9 leaves no task over 200 ms on the page with the machine loaded, measured as that guard measures a click. [review 2026-10-14 D-3, measured on the `load-health` S3 tree]
last_body: - [ ] **Divide the text step and the edit's own task on the drone-swarm v9 model.** Since `ui-small` S4 an edit's recompute yields to the page between its steps (`recomputeSteps`), but three tasks stay whole. The serializer (`serializeUserModelSignals`, `src/text`) writes the one root in a single pass: 40 to 90 ms at load about 4, up to about 180 ms at load 25. The edit's own task (the undo snapshot `model.toJSONWhere` plus the SDK update) takes 54 to 109 ms warm, up to about 296 ms at load 25. The last step (the results set plus the synchronous `buildDiagram`) takes 90 to 156 ms at load 25. Left: a step-wise serializer, an idle-time undo snapshot, and the diagram build as a separate task. Ruled permanent 2026-11-05 (the rollup 'Abstentions left (parallel machines and Simulate)' item (6)): incremental validation (unsound for cross-element rules), a worker serializer (a model transfer per edit costs about what the write does), and the cold first edit (238 ms). Done when no task of an edit and its recompute is over 200 ms at load 25. The `palette-checks` step 4 bound (200 ms) has a thin margin on slower CI cores: if the first CI run is red, make the assertion relative. [ui-small S4, review 2026-10-14 D-3]

first_title: List the elements of different owners in the order the text gives them
first_body: - [ ] **List the elements of different owners in the order the text gives them.** The page and every copy of its model (the checks worker's, Undo's, Save's) now list each owner's children in the order the owner holds them, but elements of different owners stay in the order they were added, by a load, a creation or a drag (`Model.adoptSerialOrder` and `inSerialOrder`, `src/core/model.ts`), while a terminal over the saved text reads them from top to bottom. So the two can disagree on whatever goes by the model's order across owners: the order of `reach` and `check-behaviour` rows, and a choice of the first of several, such as the first transition out of an `initial` when the transitions have different owners. Probe: `package P { package Q1 { state def M1 { state a; state b; state dead1; transition t1 first a then b; } } package Q2 { state def M2 { state x; state y; state dead2; transition t2 first x then y; } } }`; drag `Q1` out of `P` and back in: the Text view lists `Q2` first, and `reach` on the saved text reports M2's rows first, while the page and the worker report M1's first (measured on the `load-health` S2 tree). No drag is needed: a machine `M0` created in `Q1` after the load is reported after M2 on the page and in the worker, and before it by the terminal. Fix: list the user's part in containment pre-order after each edit, at a measured cost on the drone-swarm model (a load is not in pre-order: 1,030 of its 3,823 user elements would move), or order the rows by the text. Done when the probe's page, worker and terminal rows come in one order. [review 2026-10-14 D-1, the S2 review]

titles: Keep each owner's child order in a collaboration room
first_title: Keep each owner's child order in a collaboration room
first_body: - [ ] **Keep each owner's child order in a collaboration room.** A room keeps the model's elements in a `Y.Map` (`src/collab/model-doc.ts`), and a peer rebuilds the model from it in ways that lose the order an owner holds its children in. `reconcileModelFromDoc` creates the elements it is sent last to first, so a batch of new elements in one peer (one transaction, or a reset: Apply, Import, Undo, Redo) reaches the others reversed: three parts `a, b, c` made in one transaction read `c, b, a` on the other peer, and a reset to `x, y, z` reads `z, y, x`. And a peer that joins loads the model in the map's key order (`serializeFromDoc`), where a drag changed only the element's owner: after `toA` of `start, A, B, toA, toB` is dragged out of its machine and back in, the room holds `start, A, B, toB, toA` and a peer that joins then holds `start, A, B, toA, toB`, and walks `toA` out of `start` first. Its Text view differs, and a composite with no `initial` can enter another state. A peer present at a drag takes it in as a move, and lists its model as the mover does (`load-health` S2). Fix: create in the map's order, and carry the child order in the document (an order key per element, or a `Y.Array` of child ids per owner). Done when a test shows every peer's children in the mover's order after a batch, a reset and a drag followed by a join (measured on the `load-health` S2 tree). [review 2026-10-14 D-2, the S2 review]

titles: Walk a step written over inherited states
first_title: Walk a step written over inherited states
first_body: - [ ] **Walk a step written over inherited states.** Since `e0d8040` a control edge written outside a machine's region that touches one of its states refuses the machine (`machine-boundary`, `docs/06` §8.6). A specialisation that adds a step over inherited states (`package W2 { state def Base { state a; state b; state c; transition ab first a accept go then b; } state def Derived :> Base { transition bc first b accept more then c; } }`), or a typed usage that does, therefore refuses both `Base` and `Derived`, where `5943654` walked `Base` alone. Fail-closed by design. Fix: a reading that walks the two together. [O1 S3]
last_body: - [ ] **Walk a step written over inherited states.** A control edge written outside a machine's region that touches one of its states refuses both machines (`machine-boundary`, `docs/06` §8.6, §8.14): `state def Derived :> Base { transition bc first b accept more then c; }` and `exhibit state m : Modes { transition ... }` refuse `Base`/`Modes` and the specialisation. Kept on purpose: the interpreter reads a machine's own region only, so a run of `Derived` has no state and a run of `Base` never takes `bc`, and a joint walk would claim runs no simulator takes. Done when `regionDescendants` and `regionTransitions` of a specialisation or typed usage list the inherited states and transitions for the walk AND the interpreter together (ids, `hierarchyPath`, atoms, the edge census, what a redefined state or transition means, the properties a base carries, the names a report prints), with the witness replay green over them. first_title: What the livelock rows still lack

first_title: Read through a part-valued binding
first_body: - [ ] **Read through a part-valued binding.** `bind pp = top.a`, where `a` is a part, equates the two parts, so `pp.load` is what `top.a.load` is. No surface reads through it, and all four agree on the wrong value (since 5943654; found by the review of the O2 S3 step). Probe (`ppshallow`): `package PPS { part def T0 { attribute load : ScalarValues::Real default = 1.0; } part def T1 { attribute L : ScalarValues::Real default = 1.0; part a : T0; bind a.load = L; } part top : T1 { attribute :>> L = 50.0; } part pp : T0; bind pp = top.a; constraint pT { pp.load >= 40.0 } constraint pF { pp.load <= 5.0 } }`: `sysml-check` and `verify` read `pT` violated (1 vs 40) and `pF` held, where `pp.load` is 50, so `pT` holds and `pF` is violated; `capp` is the same shape past the 32-usage cap. Fix: follow a part-valued binding in `boundSourceIn` and the connector components, or abstain on it on every surface, and pin both probes in the four-surface table. Done when `pT` reads T and `pF` F on all four surfaces (or both abstain with a stated reason), and `sysml-check --strict` agrees with `verify`. [O2 S3]

titles: Exit a transition to the least common ancestor of its source and target
first_title: Exit a transition to the least common ancestor of its source and target
first_body: - [ ] **Exit a transition to the least common ancestor of its source and target.** `stepConfig` (`src/semantics/mc/config.ts`) exits only to the source's level (`exitTo(choice.level)`) and enters the target on top, as `runStateMachine` does, so a step from a substate to a state outside its composite leaves the composite active (`[C0, Idle]`). A `state C0` atom then holds at `Idle`, and a property can be refuted by a run that holds only because `C0` was never exited: on `Idle -go-> C0`, `C0 { a -x-> b; b -back-> Idle }`, absence of `state C0` after `back` is FAIL (`verification/refuted`, exit 1) at `Idle`, where UML's reading holds (`38c8d0b` does the same). Each round trip also stacks one more state: one composite of two substates reaches the depth bound and every reach list is withheld; five of four reach the configuration bound (`docs/06` §8.9). UML exits to the least common ancestor. A fix changes `simulate` and every verdict on such a machine; none in the gate corpus or v9 (`nest2-into` is refused). Fixtures that rely on it: `heavyMachine` (`palette-checks.spec.ts`) and `hierarchical(…, exits)` (`checks-registry.test.ts`). Opus class: it changes semantics and a false verdict exists now. [O7 S1]

titles: Read a step into a machine's own root, or into a node under an action
first_title: Read a step into a machine's own root, or into a node under an action
first_body: - [ ] **Read a step into a machine's own root, or into a node under an action.** Since O8 S1 a step exits to the least common ancestor of its source and its target (`docs/06` §8.10). A step whose target sits in no chain of the machine's states has none: into the machine's own root (`transition t2 first b accept back then M;` inside `state def M`), or into a node written under an action (`then act::inner`). The walk refuses such a machine (`step-outside-states`). The interpreter still reads the step the old way: on the flat path it stands at the root, or at the node under the action, with nothing more offered; on the hierarchical path it restarts at the initial state with the source's composite stacked under the root (`[C, M, a]`). The guide says so ("A step out of a composite leaves it."). Done when these targets have a reading (a step into the root restarts the machine at its initial state, with or without the root's own phases) that the walk and the interpreter share, or the simulator refuses them too. Fail-closed; no corpus model or v9 holds one. [O8 S1]

first_title: Make the palette's worker E2E independent of a one-second walk (optional)
first_body: - [ ] **Make the palette's worker E2E independent of a one-second walk (optional).** Since O8 S1 no text machine of a drawable size reaches the configuration bound, so `heavyMachine(6, 35)` (`palette-checks.spec.ts`, 'a state-machine check runs in a worker') reaches the depth bound in about a second. titles: Compare the stack in the witness replay, not only the leaf (optional)
first_title: Compare the stack in the witness replay, not only the leaf (optional)
first_body: - [ ] **Compare the stack in the witness replay, not only the leaf (optional).** `replayWitness` (`src/semantics/mc/patterns.ts`) compares each step's resting leaf. A walk stack that holds an enclosing state the interpreter never entered would still replay; the differential CASES hold three flat-path machines that would catch such a split today. Rebuilding the interpreter's stack from `visited` and `fired` and comparing it with the trace's `stack` closes it in the replay itself. [O8 S1, review]
last_body: - [ ] **Compare the stack in the witness replay, not only the leaf (optional).** `replayWitness` (`src/semantics/mc/patterns.ts`) compares each step's resting leaf. The interpreter does not expose its stack: `activeStates` is the final leaves, and `visited` records what a step enters, never what it exits, so a stack rebuilt from them cannot catch a state the walk keeps and the interpreter left. Fix: `runHierRegion` records each fire's active stack (an optional `StateFire.stack`, which moves `executionReport`'s payload), and the replay compares it with the trace's `stack`. The differential CASES' three flat-path machines catch such a split today. [O8 S1, review; behaviour-rest S2]

titles: Stop an in-page solver check from stalling or tearing the page
first_title: Stop an in-page solver check from stalling or tearing the page
first_body: - [ ] **Stop an in-page solver check from stalling or tearing the page.** N6 S4 runs the five solver checks in the page behind a queue and a mutex. Left: Cancel drops the answer but cannot stop z3, so the check ends at its own time budget and a Run started meanwhile queues behind it; a model edit during a run can give a torn read across awaits (the result lands against the click's revision and shows stale; documented, not snapshotted); a z3 module that dies in the page (the finalizer race, or a hang) keeps the bundled async-mutex held until the page is reloaded, because the mutex watcher is not wired into the esbuild-bundled entry; an in-page check keeps no evidence record (`verify --record` is terminal-only); the encoding cost (`obligationsOf`, script building, `resolveFreeFeatures`) runs on the page thread and is not measured on v9, with no long-task guard over solver checks; the `bounds` check's degraded path has no test of its own; and the isolated E2E fails if the run sets `SYSPROSE_NO_ISOLATION=1`. [N6 S4, review]
last_body: - [ ] **Stop an in-page solver check from stalling or tearing the page.** N6 S4 runs the five solver checks in the page behind a queue and a mutex. Left: Cancel drops the answer but cannot stop z3, so the check ends at its own time budget and a Run started meanwhile queues behind it; a model edit during a run can give a torn read across awaits (the result lands against the click's revision and shows stale; documented, not snapshotted); an in-page check keeps no evidence record (`verify --record` is terminal-only); the encoding cost (`obligationsOf`, script building, `resolveFreeFeatures`) runs on the page thread, is not measured on v9, and has no long-task guard over solver checks. Cancel and the long-task guard each need a bridge or measurement change, more than 150 sound lines. [N6 S4, review, ui-pass S1]

titles: Move the first Apply's parse off the page (P3, the rest)
first_title: Move the first Apply's parse off the page (P3, the rest)
first_body: - [ ] **Move the first Apply's parse off the page (P3, the rest).** N6 S5 builds the Chevrotain parser while the page is idle after the Text view opens, so the first Apply no longer pays the ~1.3 s build; the parse itself is still on the page and synchronous (`applyText`, `typedTextFirst`). Left: a worker parse needs an Apply that is in flight (the buffer edited during the parse, Undo and carried ids across the wait, the `ParseResult` rebuilt on the page, a page fallback); callers that parse before the Text view has been opened still pay the build at their click (opening a `.sysml` file, and the Drive guard's `typedTextFault` before the Text view mounted), and would need a second trigger such as the Open menu; and the warm-up is best-effort, covered only by a unit test with injected dependencies, with no E2E that the stall happens once. [N6 S5, `docs/UI-ROADMAP.md` P3]
last_body: - [ ] **Move the first Apply's parse off the page (P3, the rest).** N6 S5 builds the Chevrotain parser while the page is idle after the Text view opens, so the first Apply no longer pays the ~1.3 s build; the parse itself stays on the page and synchronous (`applyText`, `typedTextFirst`). Ruled permanent 2026-11-05 (the rollup 'Abstentions left (parallel machines and Simulate)' item (6)): moving the parse into a worker (the gain is 4-9 ms warm against five new ways for the page to differ from its text) and the parser build itself. Left: callers that parse before the Text view has been opened still pay the build at their click (opening a `.sysml` file, and the Drive guard's `typedTextFault` before the Text view mounted); the warm-up needs a second trigger on the Open menu, the file chooser and the text buffer paths, and it is best-effort, covered only by a unit test with injected dependencies, with no E2E that the stall happens once. [N6 S5, `docs/UI-ROADMAP.md` P3]

first_title: Name an unnamed nested redefinition's context row alike on every surface
first_body: - [ ] **Name an unnamed nested redefinition's context row alike on every surface.** A context that is an unnamed redefinition is named `... in q::«PartUsage»` by the check and numeric surfaces and `... in q::r` / `q::p` by the literal and SMT engines (RF, RF2, RF3, CI1; the new `dt_*_deep` files), and a model like RB5 with a relation on P gets two check rows named `P::c in q1::p` (a specialiser reading and the group's enclosing-assert row), which makes the four-surface harness throw (pre-existing at aac38fd). last_body: - [ ] **Name an unnamed nested redefinition's context row alike on every surface.** A context that is an unnamed redefinition is filed by element id (`... in q::«PartUsage»`) on the check and numeric surfaces and by instance path (`q::p`, `q::r`) on the literal and SMT engines (RF, RF3, CI1, the dt_*_deep files). The four-surface harness therefore keys them as two rows, each abstaining or agreeing, so a unified name needs the check's context rows to carry the instance path (their ids, anchors and the numeric `context.contextId` change) and a re-pin of about 40 table rows. titles: A state def used as a state's type is not lone (optional)
first_title: A state def used as a state's type is not lone (optional)

titles: List what a load binds later in the order a terminal binds it, on the page and on every peer of a room
first_title: List what a load binds later in the order a terminal binds it, on the page and on every peer of a room
first_body: - [ ] **List what a load binds later in the order a terminal binds it, on the page and on every peer of a room.** After an edit the page lists the user's declarations in the order the text gives them (`Model.adoptSerialOrder`, `src/core/model.ts`), and each owner's children come in one order on every peer of a room (`src/collab/model-doc.ts`). But a typing, specialisation, redefinition or implicit feature keeps its place among the others: one made in the app (Properties' Type field, a line drawn with the palette) is listed after every one the model had; one whose element a drag puts elsewhere in the text, or that a project, model JSON or branch stored in another order, stays where it was. A terminal over the saved text binds them in the order their declarations come. In a room, a peer that joins lists them in the order the room's document lists its keys, and a peer present after a reset (Apply, Import, Undo, Redo) keeps them where it had them. So a check that goes by them (`where-used` over a definition) can list its rows in another order than a terminal, and than another peer. Probes: (a) `package X { part def D { attribute a = 1; constraint c { a <= 0 } } part u1; part u2 : D; }`, type `u1` as `D` in Properties: the page gives u2, u1 and a terminal u1, u2; (b) `package X { part def D {...} package A { part u1 : D; } package B { part u2 : D; } }`, drag A out and back in: the page gives [u1, u2] and a terminal [u2, u1], and the same after the stored project is reopened (the same at 87e8c0f). Fix: list them in the order the parser's binding pass makes them (`:>`-family first, then `:` typings, then connector chains, each in the order of their declarations), measured to leave every load where it is, or order such rows by the text; carry that order in the room's document t
last_body: - [ ] **List what a load binds later in the order a terminal binds it, on the page and on every peer of a room.** Done by fence-coremodel, fence-order and core-pass: where-used, the impact closure, SDK traverse, REST relationships, the impact graph and the specialisers a finding names list in text order, and so do Properties' Types and Specializations lists, a table's Type cell, the diagram's subject grouping and the 3D shape inference (Model.typesInBindOrder and Model.specializationsFrom: the colon-greater family, then typings, then redefinitions). These lists use a fixed order that does not depend on the order the relationships were made in (the order where-used uses); it is not the terminal's `typesOf` listing, and no single sort key matches the terminal's raw listing (s1-spec lists the typing before the redefinition, a def-body `:>> p : P2` the reverse). What stays: (1) Model.typesOf, which the readings walk, still lists in the order the model lists the relationships, so a typing made in the app beside a subsetting or redefinition reads in another order than in a terminal. The order scope in bind.ts unreadScopes fences the shapes where the order decides a name, so no cell has been seen to differ (140 generated models). typesOf stays unsorted pending a user decision: sorting it changed a pinned abstention into a decided reading (test/unit/semantics.evaluate-model.test.ts 'abstains where no one element stands for an instance...', around line 6856, model `part def Q2 :> Q { part :>> p : P2; }` with `P2 :> P { attribute :>> extra = 9.5 }`: generic and G::q2::p went from unknown to violated, which is the KerML reading since P2::extra redefines P::extra, but it widens a verdict; decide the abstention, or keep it). Other consumers read `typesOf()[0]` the same way: consiste

titles: Resolve two peers' moves that hold two elements in each other
first_title: Resolve two peers' moves that hold two elements in each other
first_body: - [ ] **Resolve two peers' moves that hold two elements in each other.** In a collaboration room, two peers who at the same moment each move one of two elements into the other (`X` into `Y` on one peer, `Y` into `X` on the other) leave the room's document holding `X` under `Y` and `Y` under `X`. Each peer refuses the move that would close the cycle (`Model.reparent`, `reconcileModelFromDoc` in `src/collab/model-doc.ts`): one holds `X` under `Y` with `Y` at the top level, the other `Y` under `X` with `X` at the top level. A page that joins as the app joins (`connectCollab`: its own model bound to a new document, then the room synced in) holds the pair as one of the two does. A model bound to a document that already holds the room (the API's `bindModelToDoc`, through `serializeFromDoc`) holds each under the other, reachable from no root: neither shows in its tree, and its text drops both and all they hold. Moving either element again does not end it: the peer that refused keeps its own reading, because its own edit is never taken back in from the document. An Apply, Import, Undo or Redo by any peer brings every peer to that peer's tree (USER-GUIDE section 9 states it). Fix: break such a cycle the same way on every peer and on a join, for instance by putting the member with the lowest id at the top level. Done when both peers, a page that joins and a model bound to the room's document hold the pair alike, both in the tree. [collab-order S2]

titles: Keep the collaboration relay up on a model with the full library
first_title: Keep the collaboration relay up on a model with the full library
first_body: - [ ] **Keep the collaboration relay up on a model with the full library.** `scripts/collab-server.ts` caps a message at 10 MiB and sets no `error` handler on a socket, so a larger message kills the relay process (`RangeError: Max payload size exceeded`, an unhandled `error` event) and drops every room on it. A peer's first message carries the whole document, standard library included. For the drone-swarm v9 model that is 10,769,168 bytes at 87e8c0f and 10,845,744 bytes with the places `collab-order` adds; a probe on a scratch port confirmed that a v9 room kills the relay. The app's sample model with the library is 9,799,148 bytes, about 686 KB under the cap, which is why the children of the library's owners get no place until one of them moves. Fix: on a socket error close only the offending connection, and keep the standard library out of the room's document (every peer loads it), or raise the cap, or split the message. Done when a room over v9 syncs between two pages (E2E). USER-GUIDE section 9 states the limit. Pre-existing. [collab-order S2]

titles: Make a reset in a collaboration room cost what it changes (optional, measure first)
first_title: Make a reset in a collaboration room cost what it changes (optional, measure first)
first_body: - [ ] **Make a reset in a collaboration room cost what it changes (optional, measure first).** An Undo, Redo, Apply or Import in a room clears the room's document and writes every element again, library included. On v9 with its library, the editing peer's reseed plus one other peer's reconcile take about 28 to 30 s in node on a quiet machine (80 to 100 s at load 30 to 35), at 87e8c0f and at `collab-order` alike. Pre-existing. [collab-order S2]

titles: Read a subsetting usage in an instance that redefines what it subsets
Read the subsetted feature where an instance redefines a usage that subsets it
first_title: Read a subsetting usage in an instance that redefines what it subsets
first_body: - [ ] **Read a subsetting usage in an instance that redefines what it subsets.** `part def W { part p1 : T0; part p2 :> p1; constraint c { p2.load <= 5.0 } }` with `part w : W { part :>> p1 { attribute :>> load = 50.0; } }`: every w's p2 is one of w's p1s (load 50), but the walk reads w's p2 as W's own, a fresh T0 (1). So `W::c` files no row for w, and `constraint k { w.p2.load <= 5.0 }` reads T/T/T/T. A `satisfy RF by p2` written in W files no row for w either, and `verify` exits 0 (sa7, sa3 in per-instance-rest-scratch/branch-review/p; SA5's W-level reading is F). Read p2 through what the instance's p1 is, or put a usage that subsets a feature an instance redefines into `satisfierTaint`'s narrowing (and `satisfierOtherwise` for a satisfier) so that its rows abstain. Done when sa7's k and `W::c in w`, and sa3's satisfaction in w, read F or abstain on all four surfaces. A false pass. [per-instance-rest review]
last_body: - [ ] **Read the subsetted feature where an instance redefines a usage that subsets it.** RV1: `part def W { part p1 : T0[1]; part p2 :> p1 [1]; constraint c { p1.load <= 5.0 } }` with `part w : W { part :>> p2 { attribute :>> load = 50.0; } }`. w's p2 is its only p1, so `w.p1.load <= 5.0` is false, but it reads T/T/T/T; W::c reads T, the reversed `k1R` reads F/F/F/F, and strict reports a false violation. This was already so at 84fb971 (probe subsetting-pass-scratch/wbr/rv1.sysml). Taint p1 where an instance reads a usage that subsets it otherwise and p1's upper multiplicity is 1, or abstain. first_title: Finish what table-rows left of E3 and E9, and the numeric surface's reading of an evaluated pair
first_body: - [ ] **Finish what `table-rows` left of E3 and E9, and the numeric surface's reading of an evaluated pair.** (1) E3 `h2p0` (`P::c in Q::p`) and `h2c0` (`Q::c`) read ?/?/?/? beside ref T; the check and the literal engine give a sentence of their own, but h2c0's numeric surface says only 'the solve did not converge'. titles: Read the name-scope shapes S3 left abstaining
first_title: Read the name-scope shapes S3 left abstaining
first_body: - [ ] **Read the name-scope shapes S3 left abstaining.** per-instance-rest S3 reads NX1/NX3/NX4 as KerML resolves them. It files R22B's and R27F's `c in q2` (F, `constraint-by-instance`) and R38's (`constraint-by-instance` info at q2's `ld :>> load`, since 1a8f9ca). It holds EB4/EB5/W4u's usages to their bindings (SMT inconsistent axioms), and gives an enclosed binding its `#bind` row, quoted as written. Still abstaining where KerML gives a value, each pinned in the four-surface table: (1) DY1: a context that declares a name a body of its general reads through the general's owners (q's `part :>> p { attribute L = 50.0; }` beside Q's p `:>> load = L`) reads the name nowhere, its own bodies included. Read each body by the scope of the element that writes it. (2) R38: a renamed redefinition of a bound end (`attribute ld :>> load`) is read through no binding, so `c in q2` abstains, in a sentence naming the renaming, where it is F. (3) MI2 (and MI4): one `=` and one `default` under one name from two general types (Q2's `L = 50.0`, Q3's `L default = 60.0`, on the usage itself or through a general) are read nowhere, though L is 50; read the `=` value. Since 1a8f9ca the same holds for two values that AGREE under a usage's binding copy or a valueless `:>> L;` (ME6's `part s : Q2, Q3 { bind p.load = L; }` over both `L = 50.0`; ME9's `part def S :> Q2, Q3`; md_*_same and md_*_samedef). Before, they read P's default 1 on every surface; now the agreeing pair is a `same` clash, the default gives way, and s's L and p's load abstain. Read the agreed value through the copy. MI1, MI1D and MI3 (two different `=` values) are a contradiction, rightly read nowhere, with the `#clash` filed. (4) An assert t

titles: Contain a throw in a relation's own context walk
first_title: Contain a throw in a relation's own context walk
first_body: - [ ] **Contain a throw in a relation's own context walk.** Since per-instance-rest S3 these become `internal` refusals: a throw while `instanceGroups` groups a usage, in a `groupGoalRows` row, or while `equatedParts` lists the asserted equations no surface reads (tested through `instanceIndexSeam`). A throw in `DefiningEquations.readingContexts` still ends the check; `instanceGroups`, `readInContexts` and the obligations lane's `instanceRows` all ask it. A failed asserts listing is kept for the revision, so every row abstains until the next edit, even after a transient throw. [per-instance-rest S3, A.2.9]
last_body: - [ ] **Contain a throw in a relation's own context walk.** A throw in DefiningEquations.readingContexts is contained since instance-pass (readingContextsOf: the check files one internal row, the obligations lane one refused row, instanceGroups groups none of the relation's contexts). The check's context rows, the instance index, the obligations lane's instanceRows, and bindingConflicts (evaluate-model.ts) and bindingInstanceRows (obligations.ts), which ask changingContexts directly, now contain a throw too (instance-pass review: before it, a throw there made loadModelText return no model; now bindingConflicts files one unknown row '<binding>@contexts' and bindingInstanceRows one refused row '<binding> in its other contexts'; the verify exit of that refused row, inconclusive, exit 2, was not checked end to end). Left: a failed asserts listing (equatedParts' failed) is kept for the revision, so every row abstains until the next edit, even after a transient throw. A retry inside the revision is not sound: derivations, instance groups and the other per-revision caches built while the listing failed would be mixed with the later complete one, so the fix is to drop all of them together or retry only at the start of a pass. Also unprobed: the other entry points of DefiningEquations that still call changingContexts directly (defining-equation.ts:3823 and :3832). [per-instance-rest S3, A.2.9, instance-pass]

titles: Decide whether an untyped asserted conjunction defines its equation's feature
first_title: Decide whether an untyped asserted conjunction defines its equation's feature
first_body: - [ ] **Decide whether an untyped asserted conjunction defines its equation's feature.** `attribute L default = 1.0; assert constraint { L == 50.0 and L >= 0.0 }`: decision 14 makes the bare equation `L == 50.0` the definition of L over its default, but the untyped rule reads the default of a conjunction that holds an equation and reports the assert violated (cl F/F/F/X in `rv-s3fit/p/cd2.sysml`'s U). If decision 14 covers conjunctions, that F is a false verdict on all four surfaces; if it does not, the default stands as for an inequality (U5). The typed rule already abstains on such a conjunction (CD23), which is weaker under either reading and never false. Awaits the maintainer's ruling on decision 14; until then the F stays and is pinned. [per-instance-rest S3]

titles: Make an unmarked default stand against every assertion (decision 14 amended 2026-10-22)
first_title: Make an unmarked default stand against every assertion (decision 14 amended 2026-10-22)
first_body: - [ ] **Make an unmarked `default` stand against every assertion (decision 14 amended 2026-10-22).** DECIDED by the maintainer (analysis Q1, with Q2 = soft is written as a value, tag held): a `default` is hard against every assertion; an assertion that contradicts it is reported violated, and no surface reads an assertion's value into a default. A feature WITHOUT a value keeps decision 14 (an asserted equation defines it: v9's CV-17 pattern). Soft is written as a value (`attribute :>> mass = cellCount * cellMass;` in the variant or usage) or as a valueless feature plus an equation. Why: U4 (an asserted equation replaces a default) and U5 (any other assertion is checked against it) give opposite verdicts on logically equivalent assertions: `L == 50.0 and L >= 0.0` is violated while the same two parts as two asserts define L = 50 (G1); `L >= 50.0 and L <= 50.0` is violated while `L == 50.0` defines (G3); `L = L0` stands while `bind L = L0` gives way over `L0 default = 1.0` (H2 against H2f, G2); and a soft override prints nothing on any surface (`mass default = 1.2` with `assert constraint { mass == 0.8 }`: `check` 0 errors 0 warnings, `verify --engine literal` passes `b.mass <= 1.0` at 0.8; with `=` the same model is refuted). The standard's text reads a default as hard against assertions (KerML 8.3.4.10.2, SysML 7.13.1 and 7.20.1). Work: (1) gate BOTH index builders: `assertHeldIndex` stops collecting defaults (`src/semantics/defining-equation.ts:5776`) and the enclosing rule files no assertion against a default (next to `:6310-6311`; a gate on the first alone is a no-op); typed asserts keep abstaining (`:5970-5975`). (2) The binding route: `endValue` calls `assertDefinesEnd` (`:7084`, `:7111`); an asserted value carried through a binding must not replace a default eithe

titles: Mark an obligation over a contradicted value inconclusive, and settle two disagreeing asserted equations
first_title: Mark an obligation over a contradicted value inconclusive, and settle two disagreeing asserted equations
first_body: - [ ] **Mark an obligation over a contradicted value inconclusive, and settle two disagreeing asserted equations.** DECIDED (analysis Q4 and Q5). (1) When an assertion contradicts a value (`=`, or a `default` once the entry above lands), `verify --engine literal` calls the pass "unconditional" and exits 0, and `check` exits 0 with one warning; only the SMT engine fails (exit 2; `soft-hard-defaults/p2/a1-hard-exit.sysml`). The literal engine marks every obligation over the contradicted values inconclusive (exit 2) and names the violated assertion; the `check` exit code stays. v9 must not move (its blocking gate admits no constraint violation; re-run it). (2) Two asserted equations that give one valueless feature different values are settled by position: the first written, or the local one, wins; swapping them flips `t50` between `T/T/?/X` with literal exit 0 and `F/F/?/X` with exit 1 (`reconcile/n-ab.sysml`, `n-ba.sysml`; F1 and M8), and two asserts, one in P and one in `p`, read T with `check` silent. Warn, name both equations, and abstain on every reading of that feature (`=` is order-free). (3) M11: an `assert` inside a requirement def files an abstention sentence beside a decided `t50` `F/F/F/X`. (4) One contradiction makes every SMT row of the file `X`: say so in the guide. Same file as the entry above: run after it. Opus, critical; about 50M. [soft-hard analysis Q4, Q5]

first_body: - [ ] **Make the per-instance check cheaper after an edit, and bring tree10 back under 2x.** cold-check S1 finds the connectors that join a component by connector end (358e0b7). titles: Fold the per-instance findings of a cause a definition states by a derived value, or beside another read
first_title: Fold the per-instance findings of a cause a definition states by a derived value, or beside another read
first_body: - [ ] **Fold the per-instance findings of a cause a definition states by a derived value, or beside another read.** S1 folds a violated group row into its lead only when its one read comes from a plain number literal that a definition's usage states, and putting that read back to the relation's own value mends the relation (`breakingRead`, asked once per distinct set of reads, for the first five distinct sets of a group). A row whose value is derived (`L = 2.0 * K`, PB in the PI-2 test), a default, one the line does not mend, one with a unit or `sides`, or a sixth distinct reading in a group keeps its own finding, anchored at the part. Several reads fold too when `breakingRead` names the shared read. Fix: anchor those at the shared member the value comes from, or at the instance's own line that changes it. Probes: R2/R3 in e4-deep-spec for the folded shape. [reporting-residuals S1, review]
last_body: - [ ] **Fold the per-instance findings of a cause a definition states by a derived value, or beside another read.** naming-pass S1 anchors a violated instance whose one breaking read is a derived value reached through a binding (M7: q2's `:>> K = 25.0` under Q's `L = 2.0 * K`) at the single number-literal member the instance's own elements state of what the value reads, only where no other number it reads is a redefinition outside the instance's own elements (a shared default is fine). With two such members (M7b), or a redefined one stated in a specialised definition (m7j), the finding stays at the part; that is fenced, not open. Since findings-pass S4 a no-via derived read (PB's `m2 = 10.0 - load`) is anchored at r1's/r2's `:>> K`, only where every name the derived line reads is bound and the line is a declaration outside the instance's own elements (PBu and PBr stay at the part). Since S5, instances that share a derived line fold into one finding at that line, when the one input left is a redefinition on a shared definition frame. Still open: the 'beside another read' part, and a default, a unit or `sides`, and a sixth distinct set, as before. Probes: PB and M7 in test/unit/semantics.evaluate-model.test.ts. [reporting-residuals S1, review, naming-pass S1; findings-pass S4, S5]

first_title: Name and anchor a value the instance redefines, which no read carries
first_body: - [ ] **Name and anchor a value the instance redefines, which no read carries.** a value the instance's own element redefines is not among the reads, so a finding never names or anchors at it. In redef-breaks2 (q2 has `attribute :>> L = 2.0;` plus `part :>> p { attribute :>> extra = 20.0; }` under `load + extra <= 10.0`) the finding points at `:>> L = 2.0` and names `load = 2`, though putting load back to 1 still misses (1 + 20 > 10) and `extra = 20.0` breaks it. Pinned in the PI-2 S1 test (G5) as the current, honest behaviour.
last_body: - [ ] **Name and anchor a value the instance redefines, which no read carries.** Done for a group row whose instance's own element (`readIn`) redefines a plain number literal that breaks the relation (redef-breaks2 / G5: `extra = 20.0` is named and anchored). Since findings-pass: context rows are covered (S2, B1); a derived redefinition (G5c, quoted as `(= 5.0 * K)`) and a unit-bearing literal one (GUR) are named and anchored (S3); a no-read target row is anchored at its redefinition (nb12), or at its context element where the shown feature is a line a definition shares (the P2 shape; S6). Left, sound (the finding names less, never wrong): a derived redefinition that carries a unit, such as `= 5.0 * K [kg]`, is not named, because its written quantity is not compared; a derived value whose text reads a name that a read lists is left to the read (G5d); a no-read target row whose shared-definition feature is not what breaks it is anchored at its context element, not at the own redefinition that breaks it (nb5 points at `part :>> p : P2`, not at `:>> extra = 12.0`; its message still lists the shared value first); the context sentence of a context row prefixes the name with the redefining part's name, not the instance's (G5d prints `p::p.extra = 20 misses Q::c2`). [PI-2 S1, naming-pass S1; findings-pass S2, S3, S6]

first_body: - [ ] **Report an ambiguous keyword as ambiguous (optional).** When two imported definitions answer to a keyword (a bare `#exceptional` with both VendorHints and SysproseVerification imported) it resolves to the first import in `resolveFullName`, so `contracts --keywords` and the fault-tree label depend on import order; the rule fails safe (no label). Left: an ambiguous foreign-aliased keyword (a bare #precondition two imports answer to) is not reported as ambiguous: `contracts --keywords` files it as `foreign` and never raises verification/keyword-ambiguous, and fault-tree.ts counts via hasKeyword, so an ambiguous #failureMode or #exceptional makes 'found none of' read as a plain absence. first_body: - [ ] **Read two asserted equations on the two ends of one binding as one feature's two values.** Since contradicted-value S2, two asserted equations that give one feature with no value two values leave every reading of it undecided (`contradictedDefinitions` in defining-equation.ts), but two on the two ends of one binding are not read as one: in `part def P { attribute L; attribute K; bind L = K; assert constraint cl { L == 50.0 } assert constraint ck { K == 60.0 } }` with `part p : P`, the check reports the `#bind` row violated, yet `t50 { p.L == 50.0 }` reads T/T/?/X and `k50 { p.K == 50.0 }` F/F/?/X, the literal engine exits 1, and the two swap with the values (the SMT engine's axioms are inconsistent; the same at f1f5ca5). Fix: where a binding joins two features of one element, compare the equations of both as one feature's (`joinedTo`), or have a bind conflict decided from two asserted equations seed `contradictedTaint` with both ends; pin it with its twin in the four-surface table. [contradicted-value S2 review, probe rv-s2-correct/v/bnd2-ab.sysml]

What is left is precision only: the taint (equatedTaint/spreadTaint) is per feature on all four lanes (check, literal, numeric and SMT), so a `part p2 : P` beside the meeting instance, and every other P, stay undecided on `L == 50.0` once such a binding exists. first_title: Abstain over a feature an own-sibling redefinition values (Opus, moves verdicts)
first_body: - [ ] **Abstain over a feature an own-sibling redefinition values (Opus, moves verdicts).** `validation/redefinition-own-sibling` reports `part def Battery { attribute mass default = 1.2; attribute :>> mass = 0.8; }`, but the surfaces still read it. (a) default + value: check, literal and numeric read b.mass = 0.8 (`heavy` refuted, `light` held) while SMT answers inconsistent-axioms; (b) value + value: every surface already abstains, with a check conflict row; (c) a valueless redefinition over a default: all four read the default; (d) a valueless declared feature with a valued redefinition: all four read the redefinition's value. titles: Read assert not constraint c { ... } as the negation
first_title: Read assert not constraint c { ... } as the negation
first_body: - [ ] **Read `assert not constraint c { ... }` as the negation.** `part def P { attribute load : Real = 50.0; assert not constraint c { load > 10.0 } }` reads T on all four surfaces, but `c` holds at load = 50, so the negated assert is violated; the instance row of P::c in a binding-carried instance reads T the same way. A silent pass of a model that contradicts itself, identical at the base. Probes review-2026-10-14/wave3-probes/contradictory-models/h1.sysml, h2.sysml. Done when the negated assert is checked, or the form is refused with its own finding. [contradictory-models S1 review]
last_body: - [ ] **Read `assert not constraint c { ... }` as the negation.** Since numeric2 S1 a negated clause (also `require not`, `assume not`) whose body is one expression is read as the plain clause over `not (body)` on every surface, the same clause `assert constraint c { not (...) }` writes, and the save writes it back as `assert not constraint c { body }` (the element keeps `negated`; pinned neg-assert-h1/-rev, h2/-rev, family; hand oracle 280 models x both text orders: 0 wrong decided cells, 0 differences from the workaround spelling). Since solver2 S4 the body may also hold comment, `doc` and attribute members (an attribute with a `=` value or none, typed at most): they are mapped as the plain clause maps them and only the expression is negated, so `assert not constraint c { attribute y = 2.0; load > y }` reads as `assert constraint c { attribute y = 2.0; not (load > y) }` (pinned neg-assert-members/-rev; hand oracle 404 models over both text orders: 0 wrong decided cells, 0 differences from the workaround spelling). Still refused: a bodiless clause, a specialising one, `assert not requirement`, and a members body holding a nested clause, part, calc or `default` member (ruled permanent: see design-solver-entries (c) 2-3). [contradictory-models S1 review; fence-assert-not; numeric2 S1; solver2-pass S4]

first_body: - [ ] **Keep a redefinition on the more specific feature when an edit dissolves the join that kept it off it.** A redefinition kept off a more specific feature by a join an edit dissolves stays on the base feature, written by its path; the same names written by hand land on the more specific one, so page and file differ. Cases: a sibling renamed away from the name a `:>> M` is known by, a typing changed, a sibling on the redefinition's line deleted, a named redefiner (`M2 redefines N`) whose blocking sibling is deleted, and an explicit `:>> M2` that a feature renamed into `M2` moves to Q::M (Save writes it as `:>> M`; the hand reading of that collision itself depends on text order). Needs the name the author wrote kept on the Redefinition edge so an edit re-resolves it. An unnamed `:>> K2` over a named redefiner is also saved as the farthest base name (`:>> N`), as prescribed: 105 of 400 random models change text, targets identical. A redefinition whose target has no printable name left is dropped on settle (deliberate; decide whether to keep the edge and abstain with a reason sentence instead). Rows redef-target-renamed-away(-rev)(-q). Seen by the property oracle: sequences 184 and 5068 of the store.reducers generator. [redefinition-target S2]

first_title: Commit a name typed in the Properties box on blur or Enter, not per keystroke
first_body: - [ ] **Commit a name typed in the Properties box on blur or Enter, not per keystroke.** `Properties.tsx` calls `updateElement` on every keystroke, so an unrelated sibling typed Z, M, M2, M2x passes through a prefix that collides with a `:>> M`; the settle moves it to Q's M for good and the final names no longer match the same names written by hand.
