titles: Settle an implicit end copy through its whole life, not only on a retype
first_title: Settle an implicit end copy through its whole life, not only on a retype
first_body: - [ ] **Settle an implicit end copy through its whole life, not only on a retype.** The store's settle moves an implicit end copy in place on a retype (`endCopyLanding`), and these cases still differ between page and file: (a) a copy whose name nothing its owner inherits bears any more (after a retype, delete or rename) stays on the feature it redefined, so the page keeps proving through it while the saved file reads `bind p.load = L` with L unresolved (dropping the relationship alone is not enough: a later retype back onto a type that has the name makes the file re-create it while the page copy has none); (b) deleting the feature a definition-level `bind` ends on removes the binding but leaves its copies (Q1::p, Q1::p::load), and usage copies then redefine the debris where the file has Q::p and P::load (review-2026-10-14/wave3-probes/redefinition-target/debris.sysml; fuzz sequences 1024, 1254, 1314, 1372 of FZ_DEFBIND=1 FZ_FIRST=1000 FZ_N=400 FZ_STEPS=4); (c) renaming the feature a copy redefines leaves the copy under its old name (page r0::L -> Q1::Zz, the file makes r0::Zz; review-2026-10-14/wave3-probes/redefinition-target/rncopy.sysml, rncopy2.sysml; sequence 1360); (d) the mapper lands the copy of a definition's bind over a general definition's copy by text order (D2 :> D3 both with `bind ... = N`: D3's copy if D3 is written first, Q0's N if D2 is), so page and file cannot agree for both orders; decide which order the mapper takes. Fix direction: settle the copy to the name the mapper gives it or drop a copy no binding holds. Probes: review-2026-10-14/wave3-probes/redefinition-target/probe-stay.test.ts, probe-stay2.test.ts, probe-copy.test.ts. [redefinition-target review, re-review]

titles: Settle a redefinition on the routes that skip the store
first_title: Settle a redefinition on the routes that skip the store
first_body: - [ ] **Settle a redefinition on the routes that skip the store.** The store follows a removal on every route (Delete key, palette, `deleteElement`, `window.sysml.delete`/`commit`, `model.remove`, a peer's removal in `reconcileModelFromDoc`) for an explicit redefinition, and a REST commit follows the delete of a Redefinition target (`followRedefinitionRemovals`). Not followed: (a) a REST commit that deletes or retargets a FeatureTyping or Specialization leaves each `:>>` where it was (fix: in `createCommit` collect the working copy's events and call `redefinitionsDirtiedBy` and `settleRedefinitions` once after `applyChange`; probe review-2026-10-14/wave3-probes/redefinition-target/probe-resttyping.test.ts); (b) a delete through `window.sysml.model`, a peer or a REST commit leaves an implicit end copy where `Model.remove`'s walk put it, where the store's settle would put it elsewhere (Q3's L deleted under `part r : Q2, Q3 { bind p.load = L; }`: page reads r1, the file r50; probe review-2026-10-14/wave3-probes/redefinition-target/probe-copy.test.ts); (c) raw `window.sysml.model.update/create/reparent` calls are not settled at all; (d) a collaboration peer does not settle its own model and relies on the sender's settle events arriving as edits (not exercised with two live clients). Done when the planner's after-step runs the shared settle (copies included) and a REST commit settles every edit. [redefinition-target S2, re-review]

titles: Make a rename that gives two features of one owner one name, or a retarget the text cannot name, page-equals-file
Make two features of one owner under one name, and a hand-retargeted redefinition, page-equals-file
first_title: Make a rename that gives two features of one owner one name, or a retarget the text cannot name, page-equals-file
first_body: - [ ] **Make a rename that gives two features of one owner one name, or a retarget the text cannot name, page-equals-file.** Two features of one owner under one declared (or effective) name cannot be told apart by any text that names them: a redefinition aimed at the second is saved by a path that finds the first, so page and file can differ, and the editor does not refuse or rename. The same holds for an SDK `updateElement` that retargets a Redefinition edge to a feature the text cannot name from its scope (a nested anonymous part; seeds 5001 and 5439 of the extended generator, rc2/prop.probe.ts), and for the settle of an implicit copy reached by a chain through an explicit owner, which uses the mapper's head rule where the mapper used the non-unique chain rule (they differ only where two unrelated types of the owner each bear the name; not once in 8,000 sequences). The property test stops at such a state. Done when the editor refuses or renames, or the reading is ruled permanent with a sentence. [redefinition-target S2]
last_body: - [ ] **Make two features of one owner under one name, and a hand-retargeted redefinition, page-equals-file.** fence-editor fixed the order-dependent simple name (seed 5439) and the path through an unnamed part (seed 5001). What stays: (1) two features of ONE owner under one name (the saved file finds the first); (2) a Redefinition edge retargeted by hand (SDK, `updateElement`) to a feature its owner does not inherit, to a feature of another kind, or to one that makes a cycle leaves page and file redefinitions apart. A sound fence needs a stable identity between page and reparsed file (compare by place), more than 40 lines. Probes: `RC_FIRST=<seed> RC_SEQ=1 RC_STEPS=5` with review-2026-10-14/wave3-probes/fence-editor/zzprop.test.ts copied to test/unit/zzprop.test.ts, on seeds 165, 317, 400, 1327, 1406, 7220, 7430, 7436. [fence-editor S2]

titles: Take the dangling-edge scan out of Model.remove (core cost)
first_title: Take the dangling-edge scan out of Model.remove (core cost)
first_body: - [ ] **Take the dangling-edge scan out of `Model.remove` (core cost).** `Model.remove` scans every element for dangling edges, so a settle that drops many redefinitions one remove at a time costs O(N) each: deleting a base attribute that 300 redefinitions end in costs about 0.9 s on a 12.7k-element model. Find the dangling edges through the edge indexes, keeping the removal and event order. Also: a 300-deep chain with two named siblings per definition parses at 1.16 to 1.30x of 84fb971 (`chainsib300`; skip `joinsTwo`'s reach walk when no sibling redefines anything), and a retype on a usage of 1500 `:>>` settles in 343 to 453 ms. [redefinition-target S2, S3]
last_body: - [ ] **Take the dangling-edge scan out of `Model.remove` (core cost).** Model.remove finds dangling edges through a referrer index kept by create, update and remove (misc-pass), in the old scan's order and with the walk repeated while an edge listed before an edge that goes was passed over; 300 one-at-a-time removes on 13k elements went from 100 ms to 3 ms. The first remove after the index is dropped (reset, resetPreserving, adoptSerialOrder when the order changed, fromJSON) costs more than the old scan, since the index is built then: on the v9 model 26 to 34 ms against 9 to 15 ms, later removes 0.01 ms against 5 ms, and removing a definition with 30,000 incoming typings 227 ms against 52 ms; a trade-off, not a wrong answer. Left: (a) a removal that moves a Redefinition still asks relationshipsFrom, so the per-revision edge index is rebuilt each time (250 chain-member removals 62 ms at 13k elements); an incrementally kept source/target index in element order would end it, and would also be the place to fix a later dangling edge if one is found; (b) a 300-deep chain with two named siblings parses at 1.16 to 1.30x of 84fb971; skipping joinsTwo's reach walk was tried and gives no measurable gain (12 parses each, 0.40 to 0.45 s both ways), so the ratio is not from that walk; (c) a retype on a usage of 1500 :>> settles in 343 to 453 ms. Done when (a) holds with the order unchanged and (b) and (c) have a measured cause. [redefinition-target S2, S3; misc-pass]

first_title: Save an end that no name reaches
first_body: - [ ] **Save an end that no name reaches.** Save writes a binding whose end is an unnamed redefinition by its effective name (`bind p.load = L;`, `p.a.load`), but where no name reaches the end it still writes the `«eClass»` placeholder, which a terminal cannot read back (`unexpected character` on `«` and `»`) and the binding end is lost: two unnamed members of one owner that answer to the same effective name, an unnamed redefinition beside a named member of the same name, an unnamed redefinition as the head segment of the path, a redefined feature with no name. Loud, not a false verdict. Probe: `package T { part def P { attribute load : ScalarValues::Real default = 1.0; } part p : P { attribute :>> load = 50.0; attribute load : ScalarValues::Real; } attribute w : ScalarValues::Real; bind w = p.load; }` is saved as `bind w = T::p::«AttributeUsage»;`. Refuse or skip the binding with a stated reason, or give the redefinition a declared name on Save (`refTo` and `effectiveSegment` in `src/text/serializer.ts`). Also optional: now that an unnamed `:>> x` resolves to the most specific inherited feature, `refTo` could verify the effective path with `resolveFullName` instead of the one-answering-member rule. titles: Keep the standard library out of a collaboration room's document
first_title: Keep the standard library out of a collaboration room's document
first_body: - [ ] **Keep the standard library out of a collaboration room's document.** Every peer's first message and every reset carries the whole library (about 10.8 MB on the drone-swarm v9 model), and the relay takes at most 64 MiB in one message (`scripts/collab-server.ts` MAX_PAYLOAD, USER-GUIDE section 9), so a model several times the size of v9 still cannot be shared. Fix: leave the library elements out of the room's document (every peer loads it) or split the message. Done when the first message of a v9 room carries under 1 MB of library. [collab-ui S2]

titles: Make peers converge after concurrent removals in a collaboration room (pre-existing)
first_title: Make peers converge after concurrent removals in a collaboration room (pre-existing)
first_body: - [ ] **Make peers converge after concurrent removals in a collaboration room (pre-existing).** Three peers that move and remove elements at random points and then exchange their updates end with different trees in about 7 sequences of 100 (33 of 500 on collab-ui, 42 of 500 at 227d10c); a cycle is not involved, a removal that reaches one peer before or after a move into the removed owner is. Moves, creates, resets and renames alone converge (0 of 2000). Probe: `ONLY=fuzz.probe.ts N=500 OPS=mr vitest run --config vitest.scratch.config.ts` in `scratchpad/collab-ui-scratch` (copy in `~/Work/sysprose-soundness-artifacts/review-2026-10-14/wave3-probes/collab-ui/`). Wrong-answer class: peers show different models. [collab-ui review]
last_body: - [ ] **Make peers converge after concurrent removals in a collaboration room (pre-existing).** fence-collab fixed the divergence (a non-cascading remove was the cause: 81 of 500 sequences with `cascade:false`, 0 with `cascade:true`): the room binding now reads the kept children of a removed owner, and of an owner the model lacks on a seed or a reset, at the top level on every peer (0 of 4000 seeds, three peers, move/remove/create/rename/reset). What stays is core: `Model.remove(id, { cascade: false })` leaves the kept children with an ownerId no element has, and nothing moves them outside a room; reachable only through the SDK's `delete(id, { cascade: false })` (`window.sysml` and scripts). The same child survives in any snapshot (toJSON, Open, Undo, Import). A remove then a create of the same id in one transaction moves the kept child out of the re-created owner on every peer. Fix: `Model.remove` re-homes the kept children in its own transaction, or the option is refused. Probe: `m.create('Package',{id:'F'}); m.create('PartUsage',{id:'E',ownerId:'F'}); m.remove('F',{cascade:false}); m.get('E').ownerId === 'F'`. A listener subscribed after the binding sees the move before the removal (comment in model-doc.ts). [collab-ui review; fence-collab]

first_title: Stop the numeric surface reading an equation with no root, or a flat one, as solved (pre-existing, wrong answer)
first_body: - [ ] **Stop the numeric surface reading an equation with no root, or a flat one, as solved (pre-existing, wrong answer).** Identical at b635385. (1) A one-to-one equation set to a value it never reaches reads t at a far point: `2.0 ^ x == 0.0` beside `x <= 0.0` reads a t, b T at x = -30.74, and `6.0 / (x + 1.0) == 0.0` beside `x >= 0.0` reads ?/? but `solveFeasible` answers feasible, decided, with the witness x about 3e21 (review-2026-10-14/wave3-probes/numeric-curved/lens1-r5/N1..N6). (2) An exponential set equal to its asymptote reads t at |f| < 1e-9 (`5.0 == 1.5 ^ (5.0 * x - 10.0) + 3.0 + 2.0`). (3) `1.0 / x == 0.000001` beside `x >= 999999.0` reads k F and `solveFeasible` infeasible (review-2026-10-14/wave3-probes/numeric-curved/p12, R1 and R2): the absolute 1e-9 accept of a flat function in the Newton path. (4) A flat equation beside a wrong pin reads both t when the pin is within the gate. (5) `x / y == 3.0` with `y == 0.0` and `x == 0.0` gives `solveFeasible` a witness near 1e-16 though 0/0 satisfies nothing (review-2026-10-14/wave3-probes/numeric-curved/zero-over-zero-p1.sysml). Fix: withhold or reject a root-find that ends beyond the equation's tolerance only because the function tends to its asymptote (`witnessGate` does so for `x / (1.0 + x * x) == 0.6 + y`), and refuse a witness at which a divisor is within tolerance of zero. [numeric-curved]
last_body: - [ ] **Stop the numeric surface and solveFeasible reading a no-root equation reached through a further equation as solved (pre-existing, wrong answer).** fence-numeric2 fences an equation with no root, or a flat one, alone or beside an inequality, a pin or an equation that fixes the other side. What stays: `y == 6.0 / (x + 1.0)`, `z == y * 2.0`, `z == 0.0`, `x >= 0.0` reads c0, c1 and c2 imposed (t) and solveFeasible answers feasible and decided at x = 2.1e11; an asserted `y == 1.0 / x` in the same chain reads T; `y == 2.0 ^ x`, `y == 0.0000000001`, `x <= -34.0` is feasible and decided at x = -9.6e18; `z == x / y`, `z == 0.0`, `x == 1.0` is feasible and decided at y = -3.6e38. Each equation is within 1e-8 of a root alone (nearRoot takes the size over all its variables, so a runaway variable excuses any residual); the evidence of no root is joint. Pinned: fence-fn13 (t rows) and fence-fn13a (KNOWN_FALSE, both text orders); solveFeasible is not in the four-surface table. Fix: judge the witness by the minimum-norm correction of the whole touched system against the same 1e-8 relative distance; a magnitude guard is unsafe (6 of the 637 corpus models legitimately exceed 1e9 times their largest literal). Probes: fence-numeric2-scratch/review/ i01-i04, g13, f01, f03, f04, f12, b28. [fence-numeric2 review]

Cause not isolated: an unbounded walk over the library subsetting once an instance and a constraint exist. first_title: Abstentions left in the readings (rollup; sound, only weaker)
first_body: - [ ] **Abstentions left in the readings (rollup; sound, only weaker).** Each reads unknown where an answer exists; none gives a wrong answer. (1) The subsetting component fence is per usage, not per instance: the usage an instance redefines itself (w.p1 beside `p2 :> p1`), every instance of what the component's usages are features of, and a package subsetter's subsetted usage abstain even where the reading would be right (pins sub-rv1-diamond k2, sub-sa7 k1, the two satisfy rows of sat-nested-nq3; corpus model e1-subset); a sound per-instance skip needs per-context answers. (2) A bridge, chain-target or package fence fires on any member that states a value, at any depth, or whose type states one, even where the values agree. titles: Land an implicit end copy on the nearest override, whatever the text order
first_title: Land an implicit end copy on the nearest override, whatever the text order
first_body: - [ ] **Land an implicit end copy on the nearest override, whatever the text order.** fence-copy only fences it. Verified fix (scratch tree, not in this branch): make endCopyProto (src/semantics/bind.ts) accept special, the unique most specific feature the types have for the name, also when `hit` is an implicit copy and special is no copy and redefines something `hit` redefines: `if (!special || special === hit) return hit; if (redefinedClosure(model, special).includes(hit)) return special; if (hit.attrs.implicit === true && special.attrs.implicit !== true) { const of = redefinedClosure(model, hit); if (of.length > 0 && redefinedClosure(model, special).some((g) => of.includes(g))) return special; } return hit;`. Both the mapper (map-to-model.ts resolveChainEnd) and the settle (serializer.ts endCopyProtoOf) call endCopyProto, so one change keeps them equal. An equivalent pair (a nearestPastCopy helper called from the mapper and, as `nearestPastCopy(...) ?? endCopyProto(...)`, from endCopyProtoOf) in a scratch tree reads u1.N = 15 in all 6 member orders, with zero wrong cells and 24 abstentions on the 400-model generators; the mapper-only variant fails the store.reducers 300-sequence property test at sequence 42, which is why this branch ships the fence. The bind.ts variant has not been run against the property test. Done when `copy-nearest-n` (test/integration/verification.differential.test.ts) reads CNF::c12 F/F/F/F and CNF::c15 T/T/T/T and the fence in leavesOutOverride (map-to-model.ts) is narrowed to the diamond and the clash (D3 :> D1, D2 or D2, D2b). The bind.ts and serializer.ts parts need the fence-rename and fence-text owners at merge. [sweep 2026-10-31]

titles: The settle leaves a stale copy resolving after a delete or a rename (page decides, file differs)
first_title: The settle leaves a stale copy resolving after a delete or a rename (page decides, file differs)
first_body: - [ ] **The settle leaves a stale copy resolving after a delete or a rename (page decides, file differs).** (a) After the Subclassification D1 -> Q0 is deleted, D1::N is a stale copy, and a later retype of a usage whose binding copy redefines N finds that stale copy through resolveInherited and treats it as no feature; the file instead makes the copy on D3::K2 (`:>> N`). The page parts the copy and reads T/T/T/T where the file reads F/F/F/F (soak seed 91332; probe: package G { part def Q0 { attribute N default = 12.0; } part def D1 :> Q0 { attribute Zd1; bind Zd1 = N; } part def D3 :> D1 :> Q0 { attribute K2 :>> N default = 16.0; } part u1 : Q0 { attribute Zb = 1.0; bind Zb = N; } constraint c8 { u1.K2 == 16.0 } }, steps: delete Subclassification D1 -> Q0, then store.bindType(u1, D3); page pageCopies [], file u1::K2 -> D3::K2). Likely cause (not verified in session): endCopyFeature (serializer.ts) takes the first resolveInherited hit and returns undefined if it is a stale copy, instead of looking past it. (b) A name renamed away still resolves on the page through a leftover implicit copy that the settle does not part, so the page decides a constraint that names it where the file has no such name and abstains (B1: package G { part def Q0 { attribute M default = 11.0; } part def D1 { attribute K default = 13.0; } part def D2 :> D1 { attribute :>> K default = 16.0; } part def D3 :> D2 { attribute Zd3; bind Zd3 = K; } part u1 : D3; constraint c3 { u1.K == 16.0 } }, steps: retarget the Subclassification D2 -> D1 to Q0, rename D1::K to N: page T/T/T/T, file ?/?/?/?, D3::K -> D2#0 stays; B2 seed 91790 page F/F/F/F, file ?; seed 94617 raw rename route, page F F on check and numeric, file ??). After the rename the unnamed `:>> K`s effectiveNameOf is N, so the cause is in the set

first_body: - [ ] **Abstentions left in renames and name clashes (rollup; sound, only weaker).** fence-rename: (1) names unrelated to the clash inside a flagged scope are withheld along with it (e.g. `w.p.x`, or an unrelated `a = 15.0` beside a clash on `b`), because the fence is the whole owner scope, as for twins; a per-name NameClash via DefiningEquations.clashesIn would keep them (probes fence-rename-scratch/gen/g007.sysml, gen2/h000.sysml). (2) The SMT lane proves and refutes nothing anywhere on a model that holds an `order` scope. first_title: Stop deciding a feature's own value against a bound end the tool cannot resolve through a retyped redefinition (wrong answer, check/literal/numeric lanes)
first_body: - [ ] **Stop deciding a feature's own value against a bound end the tool cannot resolve through a retyped redefinition (wrong answer, check/literal/numeric lanes).** Confirmed by a read-only check of 2026-11-01 on 03e4e9f; the simple pairs are right (a `=` end against a `=` feature gives the bind-conflict message and nothing decided, nested, reversed or flat; a `default` end against a `=` feature keeps the feature's value, decision 14). The wrong answer is only where the bound end is reached through a retyped redefinition that hides a nested `=` redefinition: `part def H1 :> H { part :>> p { attribute q :>> a = 16.0; } }` with `part w : H1 { part :>> p : P2; }` and `attribute k = 5.0; bind k = w.p.a`. The tool abstains on the end (`u.w.p.a`, `u.w.p.q`, an unvalued k, a default k all read ?), yet decides `u.k == 5.0` T and `== 13.0`, `== 16.0` F, byte-identical whether q is `=` or `default`; without the retype it reports the bind conflict and decides nothing. The SMT lane answers ? (correct). Fix or fence: make the seed-keeping check abstain on k when the bound end does not resolve (treat the retyped end as unresolved), or resolve q's value through the retype. Probes: scratchpad confirm/k1/m/ (Q, R, valk-eq-fwd, m6/dfl-L2-fwd). [fence-numeric4 review, confirmed 2026-11-01]

titles: Read a single-quoted name in an expression as a reference, not a string (wrong answer on the check lane; abstention elsewhere; genericity)
first_title: Read a single-quoted name in an expression as a reference, not a string (wrong answer on the check lane; abstention elsewhere; genericity)
first_body: - [ ] **Read a single-quoted name in an expression as a reference, not a string (wrong answer on the check lane; abstention elsewhere; genericity).** `attribute 'max load' = 25.0; constraint c { 'max load' <= 10.0 }` reads ?/U/?/U where the same model with `maxload` reads F/F/F/F; `attribute 'ref'; assert constraint { 'ref' == a * b }` (satisfiable: d free, the bare spelling reads T) reads F on the check lane with a `constraint-violation` warning, because the expression lexer takes a single-quoted unrestricted name for a string literal ("String literals are not unit-aware expressions") and compares it with the number. SysML v2 spells names with spaces or keyword-like words this way, so every constraint over such a feature is unjudged and some are judged wrongly. Declarations and paths outside expressions already accept quoted names. Probes: genericity/verify/q1.sysml, q1b.sysml, q2.sysml, q2b.sysml (scratchpad). Found by the rename audit of 2026-11-02 (rename-kw experiment). [genericity audit]
